primary_meaning: darkness, night, death, or the realm of evil/Satan (as the counterpart to the east)
primary_basis: historical Christian baptismal and liturgical practice of facing west to renounce the devil
natural association of west with sunset, evening, and ensuing darkness
contrast with stronger positive east symbolism of sunrise, divine glory, and Christ (Ezekiel 43:2; Malachi 4:2; Luke 1:78)

alternatives.meaning: direction of gathering or inclusion of peoples (including Gentiles) into God's kingdom
infinite separation or complete removal of sin
direction of approach toward God's presence (Holy of Holies located westward in Tabernacle/Temple)
completion, evening, or the end of a cycle
basis: general association with sunset and close of day

notes: Cardinal directions receive largely contextual and traditional rather than explicit, uniform biblical definitions. East carries clearer positive freight, so west frequently functions as its negative opposite in Christian teaching and liturgy, yet multiple non-contradictory usages coexist without one exclusive settled meaning.
